transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because my brain just feels like it stalls out lately. I'll be at work—I'm an engineering technologist—and I'll sit there with a test report or even just a simple CAD note open on my screen for an hour. And I just... I can't decide what the next sentence should be, or even which checkbox to mark. It's like I just can't process what to do next.
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty focusing or getting started on tasks for most of your life, or is this a relatively new experience for you?

No, it's definitely new. It really started about... well, a year and a month ago. That's when they moved me into the prototype-testing role at work. Before that, I never had this kind of trouble getting things done.
Since this started a year ago, have you also noticed any changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns?
I haven't really noticed any changes with my appetite or sleep, honestly. I'm pretty sure I'm still eating and sleeping about the same as I always have.
Do you feel that this difficulty you are experiencing is directly linked to the pressures or requirements of your new role at work?

I'm not really sure. I mean, the new role is different, but I don't know if the work itself is what's causing this. It's just that the timing lines up with when I started the prototype testing. But I can't say for sure if it's the pressure of the job or just something else going on with me.
Aside from the difficulty with your work tasks, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, over this past year?
No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel sad or hopeless like that. It's really just the trouble focusing and getting things done that's been bothering me.
Outside of your specific work tasks, do you find yourself feeling excessively anxious or worried about a variety of other things in your daily life?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, like paying bills or getting to appointments on time, but it's not excessive. I don't feel constantly anxious or anything like that. It's really just the work stuff that's been a problem.
When you are struggling to focus at work, do you ever feel as though you are detached from your own body, or that the world around you feels unreal or dreamlike?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't feel detached or like things aren't real. It's really just a matter of not being able to concentrate on the tasks in front of me.
When you are stuck on those tasks at work, does it feel as though your mind is 'going blank' or is it more like you are watching yourself struggle from a distance?

No, it's not like watching myself from a distance at all. It's more just... my mind goes blank. I'll be staring at a schematic or trying to run a test, and I just can't pull the information together. The thoughts just aren't there.
When you are stuck at work, do you find yourself feeling emotionally overwhelmed, perhaps with a sense of irritability or a feeling of being 'on edge'?

No, not really. I don't feel angry or on edge, exactly. It's more just... a heavy feeling. I get frustrated that I can't do the work, but I don't feel keyed up or irritable. I just feel kind of empty and stuck.
Have you noticed any changes in how you interact with others, such as withdrawing from social situations or acting out of character since these difficulties began?

Yeah, I guess I have withdrawn a lot. At work, I actually missed a pretty important project deadline recently... and now I have to ask my coworkers to double-check my work, or even take over parts of the reports that I used to just finish on my own. It's embarrassing. And outside of work, I've mostly just stopped seeing people. I don't really do any of the normal routines that used to keep me steady anymore. I just stay home.
When you are at home staying by yourself, do you often find that you have lost interest or pleasure in the activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah, pretty much everything. I used to be really into 3D printing miniatures, but my printer has just been sitting there with the same half-finished figure on it for months. I haven't touched it. Even things that used to help me relax, like doing yoga or going for a walk in the woods... they just feel like chores now. It's just another task I have to do, not something I actually want to do anymore.

When you are away from work, such as on weekends or during your time off, do you still feel this same sense of being 'stuck' and the same loss of interest in your hobbies, or do you feel a sense of relief when you are away from the office?

It's pretty much the same on the weekends. I don't really feel any relief just because I'm not at the office. I still feel stuck, and I still don't want to do any of my hobbies. The days off just kind of blur together with the workdays. I just sit around my apartment feeling the same way I do during the week.

Looking back at your life, have you ever experienced a similar period where you felt this 'stuck,' lost interest in your hobbies, and withdrew from others, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?

No, this is the first time. I've never really felt like this before. I've had times where I was stressed or tired, but never... never this completely drained and disconnected from everything. It's all new to me.
